## Accessibility Issue: Donation form validation error not announced to screen readers **Bug ID:** `A11Y-d4e5f6a7` (instance) / `A11Y-b8c9d0e1` (pattern) **URL:** https://give.example.org/donate **XPath:** `//div[@class="form-error"]` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main/section[@id="donate-form"]/form/div[@class="form-error"]` **WCAG SC:** 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA) / 3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A) **Rule:** Manual testing / ACT Rule: 026b8e — Status message has accessible name **Severity:** Critical **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page (manual discovery during QA pass) **Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light ### HTML Snippet ```html
Please enter a donation amount.
``` ### Description When the donation form is submitted with the amount field left empty, a validation error appears visually in red above the form. However, the error container lacks ARIA attributes to expose it to assistive technology. VoiceOver users hear complete silence when the error appears and must manually navigate back to the top of the form to discover why submission failed. Sighted users see the error immediately, creating an inconsistent experience that blocks blind users from completing a core donation task. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://give.example.org/donate 2. Open VoiceOver on macOS 14 (Safari 17.4) 3. Leave the "Donation amount" field empty and submit the form 4. Observe that a red error message appears visually above the form 5. Listen to what VoiceOver announces at this moment ### Expected Behaviour Screen reader should immediately announce the validation error (e.g., "Please enter a donation amount, alert") or the input field should receive focus with an associated `aria-describedby` attribute pointing to the error message. ### Actual Behaviour VoiceOver announces nothing when the error appears. The user only discovers the failure by manually navigating back to the top of the form. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Safari 17.4 | | OS | macOS 14 | | Screen reader | VoiceOver | | Testing tool | Manual testing | ### Impact Blind and low-vision users relying on screen readers cannot identify form validation errors, leading to failed submissions without feedback. Users who rely on voice control software may also be unable to correct the error without visual guidance. This creates a complete barrier for assistive technology users attempting to complete a core conversion task. ### Suggested Fix Add `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"` to the error container, and assign it an ID that is referenced via `aria-describedby` on the input field: ```html
Please enter a donation amount.
``` ### Personalisation and Context - **Colour scheme:** Light mode (system default) - **CSS media features:** `prefers-color-scheme: light`, `forced-colors: none` - **Viewport:** 1440 × 900 px (Desktop) - **Navigation path:** Direct URL visit during monthly giving campaign QA pass - **UI state:** Form validation failed / Error message visible - **Login state:** Guest / Unauthenticated
